name: Coral bleaching
summary: No new global bleaching event declared as of 13 Nov; IUCN says most shallow reef systems face collapse risk
state: An IUCN assessment reported on 5 Nov rated about 96% of shallow-water reef ecosystems critically endangered, mainly from ocean warming and marine heatwaves (AP via WCAX). That is a long-run risk rating, not a bleaching declaration: no fifth global bleaching event or confirmed regional mass bleaching was found as of 13 Nov. NOAA's August outlook gave a greater than 70% chance of Alert Level 1 heat stress across most of the Caribbean by early November (GCRMN, 14 Aug), so the level stays Normal with an upward trend.
for_you: Reef-dependent fisheries and tourism in the Caribbean are most exposed if heat stress builds during the El Niño. Bleaching reports usually follow weeks of high sea temperatures; NOAA Coral Reef Watch publishes regional alerts.
rubric_hit: Normal: no global bleaching event in progress and no confirmed regional mass bleaching as of 13 Nov

sources.title: WCAX (AP) — Almost all coral reef ecosystems face risk of collapse in 50 years, study warns

why: Reefs support a quarter of marine species and coastal economies; mass bleaching is a direct sign of ocean heat stress.
drivers: Marine heatwaves, El Niño, warming trend.

rubric.alert: Bleaching extent at record levels with active new alerts in the past month.
rubric.watch: Global bleaching event in progress, or regional mass bleaching.
rubric.normal: No global bleaching event in progress.
